tasks.short: Send a questionnaire to departments and collect answers, interview key users, analyse answers and current document stores, and write the needs assessment.

steps.what: Document management specialist sends a questionnaire to departments and collects answers by e-mail
Document management specialist conducts needs assessment interviews with key users
Document management specialist analyses answers and current document stores in a spreadsheet
Document management specialist writes the needs assessment report

tasks.design: An online questionnaire ({OTHER}) collects departments' answers in one table instead of e-mails, and its charts plus storage reports from the document system ({DOCS}) give the first analysis. The report starts from a template with sections per department. Interviewing key users and judging needs stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers came back by e-mail and were typed into a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Online questionnaires and storage reports give data in one place.
tasks.still_hard: Departments answer late or not at all.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the workaround a department is embarrassed about.

reach.learn: Whether the questionnaire is quick to fill in.

evidence.claim: Online questionnaires collect answers in one table and chart them.

assumptions: Boundary: from the assessment planned to the report written; choosing a system is outside.
Input contract: questionnaire tool available; fallback is e-mail.
Departments fill the form in about the time an e-mail took.

incremental.description: Document management specialist keeps the questionnaire current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a few departments with long interviews; high: many departments answering online.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read change requests, configure access profiles, configure workflow procedures, adjust user interface views, test with a key user, and document the configuration.

steps.what: Document management specialist reads change requests from e-mails
Document management specialist configures access profiles per user by hand
Document management specialist configures document workflow procedures
Document management specialist develops user interface views
Document management specialist tests the changes with a key user
Document management specialist documents the configuration

tasks.design: Change requests arrive through a service desk form ({HELPDESK}) with the site, users and change type filled in. Access follows role groups synced from the HR system ({HCM}), so joiners, movers and leavers get or lose access without hand work; about 80% of access fits a standard role and the rest is still set by hand. Workflow and view templates are reused across departments. The configuration page is exported from the system. Testing with a key user stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by e-mail and access was set per user by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems take role groups from the HR system and reuse templates.
tasks.still_hard: Project teams need access outside standard roles.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who really needs to see a confidential folder.

reach.learn: Whether access is right on day one.

evidence.claim: Document systems can take role groups synced from the HR system for access.
Access must be limited to those who need personal data for their work.

assumptions: Boundary: from the change request to the configuration documented; needs assessments are outside.
Input contract: roles kept current in the HR system; fallback is per-user access.
Scenario: about 80% of access fits standard roles.
Key users' time does not change.

incremental.description: Document management specialist maintains role-to-access mappings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many project teams with special access; high: mostly standard departments.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect requirements from earlier assessments, write the functional specification, draw process and data diagrams, and review it with IT and the vendor.

steps.what: Document management specialist collects requirements from earlier assessments and notes
Document management specialist documents technical functions and specifications for the new content management system

loop.input: The numbered requirement list and the vendor's product documentation.
loop.check: Every function statement must cite a requirement number or a section of the vendor documentation, or it is dropped; the specialist edits every section.
loop.stop: One draft per section; if rejected, the specialist writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template gives headings, not how each requirement is met.

steps.what: Document management specialist draws process and data diagrams
Document management specialist reviews the specification with IT and the vendor

tasks.design: Requirements from earlier needs assessments are kept as a numbered list in the team wiki ({DOCS}), so they are not gathered from old notes. A bounded step drafts specification sections from the list and the vendor's documentation; statements without a requirement number or documentation reference are dropped and the specialist edits every section. Diagram templates speed up drawing. Reviewing with IT and the vendor stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements sat in old notes and specifications were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft sections that can be traced to requirement numbers.
tasks.still_hard: Vendor documentation is often vague about limits.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the requirement nobody wrote down.
tasks.altitude: The specialist edits specifications instead of writing them from scratch.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft specification text whose statements can be traced to requirement numbers.
Products with digital elements sold in the EU must meet cyber security requirements.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new system planned to the specification reviewed; buying the system is outside.
Input contract: numbered requirement list kept in the wiki; fallback is old notes.
Vendor and IT time does not change.
research_questions: How much of each drafted section is kept?

already_counted.description: Document management specialist edits drafted sections.

incremental.description: Document management specialist keeps the requirement list numbered and current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a new kind of system; high: a replacement of a known system.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review access logs, check sharing settings, investigate incidents, check archive and destruction lists, write the findings report, check it, and send it to the security officer.

steps.what: Document management specialist exercises security surveillance by reviewing access logs
Document management specialist checks sharing settings and external links site by site
Document management specialist investigates incidents
Document management specialist checks archive transfers and destruction lists
Document management specialist writes the monthly findings report
Document management specialist checks the final findings report
Document management specialist e-mails the report to the security officer

tasks.design: Fixed alert rules on the access logs of the document stores that send logs, about 80%, flag mass downloads, access outside a user's role and external sharing of sensitive documents ({DOCS}), so the specialist reviews flagged events instead of reading raw logs; stores without logging are still checked by hand. A sharing report lists external links and open sites, and retention reports list documents due for transfer or destruction. The monthly report fills counts from these reports, and once checked it goes to the security officer. Investigating incidents stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Logs and sharing settings were checked by hand site by site.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems report access and sharing and support alert rules.
tasks.still_hard: Older stores do not log access.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a mistake from a leak.
tasks.altitude: The specialist investigates flags instead of reading logs.

evidence.claim: Processing personal data for network and information security can rest on legitimate interest.
Monitoring staff access logs needs works council consent under national rules.
Document systems can report access and sharing and raise alerts on set rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the review period to the report sent; disciplinary follow-up is outside.
Input contract: alert rules agreed with the security officer; fallback is reading logs.
Scenario: about 80% of document stores send access logs.
Logs are used for security, not to rate staff.

incremental.description: Document management specialist tunes alert rules to cut false flags.

approvals.approved_version: The findings report as checked by the specialist in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older stores without logs; high: all stores logging.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The document management specialist keeps interviewing users, configuring workflows, reviewing specifications and investigating incidents; e-mailed answers, per-user access, specifications from scratch and raw log reading shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A specialist with more time on information security.
